clue.text: Idle figure and aggressive youth hanging around a tree on the way up

indicators.note: to hang around something is to surround it, so the youth's letters enclose the rest

parts.note: a lout is a rough, aggressive young man

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the tree's letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: the bay is a laurel tree

explanation.surface: A lazy figure and a thuggish youth loiter near a tree beside the road uphill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Idle figure' is the definition, a lazy person; 'on the way up' works because this is a down entry, so the tree is read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A layabout is a lazy idler, a person who avoids work, so an idle figure.

clue.text: Rude remarks amid stress muttered

indicators.note: amid tells us the answer sits among the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone under pressure mumbles crude comments.
explanation.definitionFit: Smut is obscene or indecent talk, the stuff of rude remarks.

clue.text: Face venomous creature needing specialist treatment

parts.note: an asp is a poisonous snake
ECT, electroconvulsive therapy, is a specialised psychiatric treatment

explanation.surface: Someone bitten by a snake needs expert medical care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Face' is a noun here, as in one face or side of a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspect is a side or facet of something, as a face of a cube or an issue.

clue.text: Salesman, one in endless celebration, getting suspension

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative

indicators.note: in places the single letter inside the shortened celebration word
endless says the celebration word loses its final letter

parts.note: a revel is a lively celebration
one is I as a Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A salesman at a party is suspended from his job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts REVEL to REVE, and I goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprieve is a suspension or postponement of a punishment, especially a death sentence.

clue.text: Jogger to step into ground

indicators.note: ground is the past tense of grind, so these letters are crushed into a new order

explanation.surface: A runner is told to stride onto the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jogger' is a memory jogger, not a runner.
explanation.definitionFit: A sticky note is stuck up as a reminder, something that jogs the memory.

clue.text: Pass by topless Italian ladies

indicators.note: topless removes the first letter, the top of a word in a down clue

parts.note: signore is Italian for ladies, plural of signora

explanation.surface: Walk past some Italian women sunbathing without tops.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass someone by is to disregard or overlook them, which is to take no notice.

clue.text: Monkey revealing part of body among second group

indicators.note: among places the body part within the letters for second

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
the arm is a part of the body
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A monkey shows off a limb in a group that came second.
explanation.definitionFit: A marmoset is a small South American monkey.

clue.text: Strain to acquire one pound for headwear

indicators.note: a word that acquires something takes it in, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: to try is to strain or test
one is I as a Roman numeral
lb is the abbreviation for a pound weight

explanation.surface: Someone strives to get a pound to buy a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A trilby is a soft felt hat with an indented crown, a type of headwear.

clue.text: Satisfying English number getting disgusted reaction

parts.note: ugh is an exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: A pleasing English song provokes a disgusted response.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is sufficient satisfies a need, as in enough food, an adequate amount.

clue.text: Provide service for heavy object, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is chosen for how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: a weight is a heavy object

explanation.surface: A waiter is asked to serve something heavy.
explanation.definitionFit: To wait at table is to serve customers in a restaurant.

clue.text: Eastern fighter with restricted allowance for going abroad

parts.note: a MiG is a Russian fighter jet
a ration is a fixed, limited allowance

explanation.surface: An eastern soldier on short rations is posted overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Emigration is leaving one's country to settle in another, so going abroad.

clue.text: Appropriate feature in snooker?

definitions.meaning: to appropriate is to take for oneself, to steal
a snooker table has six holes at its corners and sides

explanation.definitionFit: To pocket money is to steal it; on a snooker table the balls are potted into these holes.

clue.text: Woman helping to accommodate Danes?

parts.note: the Danes are not people from Denmark but Great Danes, the dog breed, housed by a woman who looks after dogs

explanation.definitionFit: A kennelmaid is a woman employed to look after dogs at a kennel, including big dogs like Great Danes.

clue.text: One taking a dip grabbing note for rest

indicators.note: grabbing means the swimmer word takes hold of the note inside it

parts.note: a bather is someone swimming, taking a dip
re is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A swimmer grabs a note and takes a break.
explanation.definitionFit: A breather is a short pause to catch one's breath, a rest.

clue.text: Figure recalled greed, perhaps, in sport

parts.note: ten is a figure, a number

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters run in the opposite direction

parts.note: greed is one of the seven deadly sins, an example of a sin

explanation.surface: A sports figure is remembered for greed.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis is a racket sport played over a net.

clue.text: Latin bus crashed in foreign city

indicators.note: a crashed vehicle is wrecked, so its letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: An Italian bus has an accident in a city overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Istanbul is the largest city of Turkey, foreign from a British setter's view.

clue.text: Record created by me in sea in France?

indicators.note: in places the French word for me inside the French word for sea

parts.note: mer is French for sea
moi is French for me, the 'in France' serving both words

explanation.surface: A diary written by someone while at sea off France.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'in France' covers both words, so the solver translates both me and sea into French.
explanation.definitionFit: A memoir is a written record of one's own life and experiences.

clue.text: Port manufactured great armour, perhaps

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port, often just Rio

indicators.note: manufactured means made up, so the following word's letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A port city produced fine armour.
explanation.definitionFit: Riot gear is protective clothing worn by police facing disorder, a kind of modern armour.

clue.text: Clear head needed by conservationists

parts.note: the pate is the top of the head
NT is the National Trust, a British conservation charity

explanation.surface: A clear-thinking leader is needed by environmental campaigners.
explanation.definitionFit: Patent as an adjective means obvious or plain, so clear.

clue.text: Beverage about to be consumed by fellow, getting half each

indicators.note: consumed by means eaten up, so the short word goes inside the word for fellow

parts.note: a gent is a fellow, a man
re means about, concerning

indicators.note: half takes the first two of the four letters

explanation.surface: A man drinks a beverage and gets half of each serving.
explanation.definitionFit: Green tea is unfermented tea, a drink or beverage.

clue.text: Man on board that is inexperienced type

parts.note: a rook is a chess piece, a man on the board
ie abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A new board member is said to be inexperienced.
explanation.definitionFit: A rookie is a novice or beginner, someone new and inexperienced.

clue.text: Effect of quake seen in backward capital? Right

indicators.note: backward says the capital and right letters are read in reverse as one run

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy

explanation.surface: Signs of an earthquake appear in a backward capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' governs both the capital and the abbreviation for right, so the whole run is read in reverse rather than the city alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremor is a slight shaking of the ground, an effect felt in a quake.

clue.text: Retire with last instalment of pension in Italian city

indicators.note: in places the final letter of pension inside the city name

parts.note: Turin is a city in northern Italy

indicators.note: the last instalment is the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A pensioner retires to an Italian city on the last payment.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn in is an idiom for going to bed, to retire for the night.

clue.text: Seize for use a new group of animals after taking firm measure

indicators.note: after taking places the later pieces after the firm and measure

parts.note: co is short for company, a firm
mm is millimetres, a measure
deer are a group of animals, a herd species

explanation.surface: A company takes a new herd after a firm measure is agreed.
explanation.definitionFit: To commandeer is to take possession of something for official or military use.

clue.text: Immense French novelist almost close to irreplaceable

indicators.note: almost says the novelist's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Victor Hugo was a French novelist, author of Les Misérables

indicators.note: close to means the end, the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A great French novelist is nearly irreplaceable.
explanation.definitionFit: Huge and immense are synonyms meaning enormous in size.

clue.text: Quantity of fish in dining area reported

indicators.note: reported means spoken aloud, so the word is chosen for its sound

parts.note: a hall is a dining area, as in a college dining hall

explanation.surface: Fish caught are reported in the dining room.
explanation.definitionFit: A haul is the amount caught at one time, especially a catch of fish in a net.

clue.text: Major route and place providing setting

parts.note: the M1 is a major British motorway, written MI in crosswords
lieu means place, as in in lieu of

explanation.surface: A main road and location make a backdrop.
explanation.definitionFit: A milieu is a person's social environment or surroundings, a setting.

clue.text: Legal body overturning core of matter in hearing

indicators.note: in places the reversed core word inside the hearing

parts.note: a trial is a court hearing

indicators.note: overturning means turning over, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: the nub is the core or crux of a matter

explanation.surface: A court body reverses the central issue at a hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'core of matter' is a phrase meaning the crux of an issue rather than an instruction to take middle letters of the word matter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribunal is a body set up to judge or adjudicate on legal disputes.
